title: Dynamic Entropy Deployment Throttler and Canary Quarantine
creator: Ananya Rao
description: Introduce an entropy-based throttling controller for progressive deployments. The controller computes an "entropy" score from multiple telemetry streams (latency percentiles, error fraction, user-cohort skew, and token-efficiency regressions) and uses that score to adapt traffic ramps, quarantine unstable canaries, and trigger automated rollback or partial pause policies. Goal: reduce false-positive rollbacks while catching real regressions earlier and containing blast radius to narrow cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes a normalized entropy score per cohort (0..100) from configured signals
Traffic ramp policies can be expressed as functions of entropy (e.g., ramp_rate = base_rate * (1 - entropy/100))
Quarantine action available: hold, partial-rollout, route-to-safe-variant, or full rollback
Integration tests exercising synthetic regressions demonstrate quarantine within 3 ramp steps for high-entropy events
Dashboards show entropy time series, cohort-level quarantine decisions, and rollback rationale
Playbook and runbook updated; on-call can override automatically enforced quarantine within console
implementation_plan: Design signal weighting and normalization: define inputs (p50/p95/p99, errors, token cost drift, user-error delta) and produce entropy score
Add a new rollout controller service in the release-orchestration component that subscribes to telemetry streams and computes entropy per cohort
Extend feature-flag platform to accept rollout-controller decisions (hold/quarantine) with signed attestations
Implement quarantine actions: traffic hold, route-to-fallback-model, cohort isolation, and enqueue rollback with justification metadata
E2E tests: synthetic traffic generator to emulate slowdowns, hallucination spikes, and cost regressions; verify controller response
Ship dashboards (Grafana) and a lightweight explainer in Console with human-readable reasoning for decisions
Gradual dogfood rollout: internal teams -> small external cohorts -> global, with observability gates and manual override
Post-rollout retrospective and tuning (weight adjustments, thresholds, noise robustness)
notes: 2025-02-21: Initial design review with PM and SRE. Agreed to include token-efficiency drift as a first-class signal because cost regressions have been missed by latency-only gates.
2025-02-24: Prototype entropy function implemented in a notebook (link below). Early tests show sensitivity to p99 spikes; need to cap p99 influence to avoid noisy rollouts.
2025-02-27: Security/Privacy check: cohort-level telemetry will be aggregated and anonymized; no raw customer payloads leave VPC in Private mode. Security reviewed by Priya Kaur, no blockers.
2025-03-01: Engineering spike produced a PoC rollout-controller service. Latency to decision under 200ms for 1k cohorts; memory footprint acceptable.

2025-03-03: Design feedback from Console team: quarantine decisions must include human-readable rationale and links to the top contributing signals. Will add a 'top_reasons' field in decision payloads.
Open trade-offs: choose conservative vs. aggressive quarantine policy. Proposal favors false negatives slightly (avoid frequent rollbacks) but quarantines narrow cohorts quickly.
Follow-ups: tuning plan for weights, add simulated annealing for threshold decay, run chaos experiments during dogfood phase.
